newsitem.title: UK: Six asylum seekers refuse fluids in British prison.
newsitem.headline: Six asylum seekers refuse fluids in British prison.

text.p: A government minister on Wednesday appealed to 17 asylum seekers detained in a British prison who have been on hunger strike for weeks to call off their protest.

"There is no good reason for detainees to be refusing either food or fluids," Ann Widdecombe told parliament. "It is clearly in their best interests to stop their hunger strike now. I urge them to do so."
In a statement, Widdecombe, a minister at the Home Office (interior ministry), said that on Monday six of the 17 began refusing to drink as well as to eat.
"A small number of the protesters have claimed to be refusing fluids. The most recent information indicates that there are six who are currently doing so," she said.
"I do not want any of these detainees to die. That is why medical attention is available, but it is up to them whether to take it up or not," she added.
Officials said the 17 are from Romania, Russia, Algeria, Angola, Nepal, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Sri Lanka, Tanzania and Zaire, but could not say how many were from each country.

Left-wing Labour member of parliament Jeremy Corbyn, who had demanded the statement, spoke of the "sense of outrage and grievance" felt by people who sought asylum in Britain and found themselves put into prison.
He said he understood one of the six was "in a very critical state indeed".
But Widdecombe said detention was "used only very sparingly indeed" with only about one percent of asylum seekers in prison at any one time.
She added that one of the inmates involved in the fluids protest had served a prison sentence for indecent assault of two children, been removed from Britain and then re-entered unlawfully.
Asylum seekers are detained if it is thought that they are likely to abscond if refused leave to remain in the country.
